intro: Prescription medications can be an effective way to treat and manage a variety of physical ailments. However, when used to treat chronic pain, anxiety, depression, and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorders, they come with a risk of abuse and misuse.

It is possible for these medications to be taken as prescribed and to receive the desired results. It is even possible for someone to take the medications as prescribed and develop a physical dependency on medications without developing an addiction to them. But what about the individuals who do develop an addiction to prescribed medications? Or those who develop an addiction after experimenting with prescription medications?

While there are some differences between an addiction to prescription medications and other substances, there are commonalities in their addiction. This includes common consequences of addiction, risk of medical health concerns, and the risk of developing mental health concerns. Rehab programs can provide you with the support, knowledge, and compassion needed to develop the foundation for your recovery.

sections.title: Why Is Prescription Drug Abuse Common?
body: Prescription drug abuse is common in our country because of the availability of medications. Prescription medications can be used to effectively treat a variety of health concerns, including pain, anxiety, and mood disorders. If medications are not taken as prescribed, be it sooner than intended or in larger doses, the individual is at a higher risk of developing an addiction.

If you have been misusing or abusing prescription medications, you may need a prescription drug rehab center in Huntington Beach. Detoxing from prescription medications can be uncomfortable, painful, and potentially be life-threatening. Detoxification programs are strongly recommended to individuals who want to stop using prescription medications because they will receive around-the-clock medical supervision and support. Call 949-649-0702 to learn more now.

sections.title: Why Are Prescription Drugs More Accessible than Other Substances?
body: Individuals who are given prescription medications, including opioids, benzodiazepines, and sedatives are at risk of developing an addiction when taking these medications. Individuals need to be mindful about the directions provided by their doctor, and be honest with their provider if they are beginning to use medications in ways other than how it was prescribed.

Prescription medications have been accessible across the country. Not too long ago, tracking software was not available for medical professionals to monitor prescriptions given to their patients, and the prescriptions that medical professionals provided. This led to an increase of the availability of various prescription medications. Even with preventative measures, there is still the availability of prescription drugs.

Some individuals are given a short-term prescription of a controlled substance and may not end up using the full amount given to them. If an individual does not know how to properly dispose of this medication, it is at risk of being taken by someone other than who it was intended for.

sections.title: How to Treat Prescription Drug Addiction
body: An important step in prescription drug treatment is detoxification. Detoxing from prescription medication can be an uncomfortable and even painful experience. Some medications, such as benzodiazepines, are associated health risks during the withdrawal process and warrant medical attention. Because of these factors, it is important that you speak with a medical professional before you stop using. Depending on your symptoms and risk factors, your medical professional may recommend detoxing on an outpatient basis, or in an inpatient rehab center.

Once you have the drugs out of your system, the real work begins. Addiction treatment programs help you understand the root of your addiction and navigate your life in recovery. This can include avoiding people that use, places you associate with using, and objects that are related to drug use.

Addiction rehab programs can help you improve life skills including communication and establishing boundaries. Learning new coping skills can also be a valuable take-away from addiction rehab programs.

If you are struggling with another mental health concern in addition to your substance use disorder, you may be eligible for dual-diagnosis treatment. Mental health concerns such as anxiety, depression, mood disorders, and personality disorders are often intertwined with addiction. At this time, research supports the practice of receiving treatment for both concerns at the same time.

If you have been misusing or abusing prescription medications, you may be eligible for inpatient treatment. This can include detoxification and residential inpatient treatment, both of which are available at Ocean Coast Recovery. Our residential inpatient rehab program ranges from 30 to 90 days and will be dependent on your unique needs. We encourage you to call 949-649-0702 to learn more about our available treatment options.
